cards.text: David is the new king over all Israel (1 Chronicles 11:3). Now we meet his mighty men, the chiefs who, together with all Israel, strengthened his kingdom, according to the word of the LORD. Friend, I once lost a tug-of-war to a rubber band in that junk drawer, so these guys already scare me.
First on the list is Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers. One man. One spear. And a WHOLE lot of opponents.

cards.question: Jashobeam wields his spear against ___ hundred men and kills them at one time.

cards.text: Next in command is Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men. He's with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gather for battle, at a field full of barley.

cards.question: When the Philistines come at the barley field at Pas-dammim, the troops hold their ground.
The troops run from the Philistines. But Eleazar and David don't. What do those two do?

answers.text: Stand in the middle of the field and defend it
Chase after the troops to bring them back
Set fire to the barley and slip away

cards.question: Eleazar and David strike down the Philistines, and the ___ brings about a great victory.

cards.text: Another time, three of the thirty chief men go down to David at the rock at the cave of Adullam, while David is in the stronghold. Philistines are camped in the Valley of Rephaim, and their garrison is at Bethlehem.
David longs for water, and he says it out loud. He wishes someone would get him a drink from one particular well.

cards.question: David wishes someone would bring him a drink of water. Where is the well he's thinking of?

cards.text: So the Three break right through the Philistine camp, draw water from that well, and carry it back to David. Friend, I've been wishing out loud for somebody to scrub my cookie sheets for YEARS, and nobody moves... because I live alone.

cards.question: The Three hand David water they got by breaking through a Philistine camp. What does David do with it?

answers.text: He pours it out to the LORD
He gives it to the troops

cards.question: David refuses to drink the water from Bethlehem because the men risked their lives to bring it.

cards.text: Then David says, "Far be it from me, my God, to do this! How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?" Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

Now meet Abishai, the brother of Joab, David's chief commander (1 Chronicles 11:6). Abishai is chief of the Three, and he wields his spear against three hundred men, kills them, and wins a name along with the Three. Three hundred. AGAIN.

cards.question: Abishai, the chief of the Three, is officially included among the Three.

cards.text: Abishai is doubly honored and leads the Three without ever being one of them. Next up is Benaiah son of Jehoiada from Kabzeel, a man of valor and a man of many exploits.

cards.question: Benaiah strikes down two champions. Which nation are they from?
On a snowy day, Benaiah goes down into a pit and kills a ___.

cards.text: A SNOWY day. Down in a PIT. With a LION. Friend, on a snowy day I hit the snooze button four times, and my bed is RIGHT NEXT to the ovens.
Then there's an Egyptian, a huge man five cubits tall, with a spear like a weaver's beam in his hand. And Benaiah goes against him with a club.

cards.question: Benaiah has a club. The huge Egyptian has a spear like a weaver's beam. How does Benaiah win?

answers.text: He snatches the spear and kills him with it
He knocks the spear away and the Egyptian runs
He calls the Three to fight beside him

cards.question: Benaiah is the most honored among the Thirty, and he becomes one of the Three.
After all his exploits, David appoints Benaiah over his ___.

cards.text: Then comes the long roll call of the mighty men, from Asahel the brother of Joab down to Jaasiel the Mezobaite, with names like Zelek the Ammonite, Ithmah the Moabite and Uriah the Hittite. I can't pronounce half these names, friend, and every one of them could beat me at arm wrestling, and my arms are a MUSTACHE.

findings.problem: The question says the troops run but Eleazar and David "don't." That rules out the wrong answer "Set fire to the barley and slip away" because slipping away is running. It also weakens "Chase after the troops to bring them back," which means leaving the field. The setup gives the right answer away by elimination.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card sets up one of the passage's big moments: Eleazar and David at the barley field. It reads as a plain list of facts with no reaction, comparison or storyteller line from Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card opens the Bethlehem well episode. It is a dry summary of places (Adullam, the stronghold, Rephaim, Bethlehem) with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a note, not a storyteller setting a scene.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This is not the passage's opening card, but it runs three sentences plus a one-word fragment. It also packs in several beats: who Abishai is, Joab's role, Abishai as chief of the Three, the three hundred men, winning a name, and the callback.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card only reacts to 11:22, which cards 3 to 5 already covered. It retells the snowy day, the pit and the lion, then adds a joke, without moving the passage forward. It also runs three fragments plus a sentence. The joke should ride along on a card that tells the next piece of the passage, such as card 7.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
